title: Early recording methods and the Roseland engagement
summary: Mute question, then how soloists had to stand away from big microphones, and the claim to be the first colored orchestra at the Roseland.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: He was using a mute there.
He told me he didn't use a mute on that.

The system of recording was different than now, you know. You had to, the soloist had to get up and walk up to there. There was big microphones sticking out. You had to get so many feet from it. You know, sometimes it would be too much and sometimes it wasn't enough. And that's kind of difficult, you know. I think we was the first colored orchestra to play appointment and engagement at the Roseland. Fifty Fweys and Broadway. That was one of the most beautiful dance palettes in America at that time.
